design_detail: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject laboratory study of single intranasal methamphetamine doses in experienced, non-treatment-seeking users; cardiovascular, subjective and cognitive measures.
can_establish: Acute dose–effect relationships under controlled conditions in this population.
cannot_establish: Effects of repeated or high-dose use; effects in inexperienced users; generalization from a laboratory setting.

sample.recruitment: Advertisement; current users not seeking treatment.
sample.selection_effects: Experienced users tolerate and respond differently from naïve users.

exposure.measurement: Administered doses (placebo, 12 mg, 50 mg [to be extracted from PDF]).
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Verified at session start [to be extracted from PDF]

outcomes.instruments: Heart rate, blood pressure; visual-analogue subjective scales; cognitive tasks [to be extracted from PDF]

analysis.power: Small sample typical of this paradigm.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Dose-related cardiovascular and positive subjective effects; cognitive performance not impaired, improved on some measures.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Sometimes cited as showing methamphetamine 'improves cognition' in general; the study shows acute effects of controlled doses in experienced users.

replication.where_it_stands: Acute performance effects of amphetamines in laboratory settings are well replicated.

what_would_settle_it: n/a for the acute question; the open questions are about chronic use.

domains.note: Order randomization [to be extracted from PDF]

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Standard human-laboratory design; small n limits precision, not validity.
